True Statement: In 1665, Robert Hooke published Micrographia, observed a thin slice of cork, and called each small space a "cell" — the first use of the word "cell" in science.
False 1: In 1665, Antonie van Leeuwenhoek published Micrographia and first used the word "cell" in science.
False 2: In 1865, Robert Hooke published Micrographia and first used the word "cell" in science.

True Statement: Robert Hooke's microscope made things look 200 to 300 times bigger than what the unaided eye could see.
False 1: Robert Hooke's microscope made things look 1000 to 2000 times bigger than what the unaided eye could see.

True Statement: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek (1660s) was the first person to clearly see and describe bacteria and blood cells; he is known as the Father of Microbiology.
False 1: Robert Hooke was the first person to clearly see and describe bacteria and blood cells; he is known as the Father of Microbiology.
False 2: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek was the first person to clearly see and describe bacteria and blood cells; he is known as the Father of Cell Biology.

True Statement: All living beings are made up of cells.
False 1: Most, but not all, living beings are made up of cells.

True Statement: A cell has three main parts: cell membrane (outer layer), nucleus (middle), and cytoplasm (between cell membrane and nucleus).
False 1: A cell has three main parts: cell wall (outer layer), nucleus (middle), and cytoplasm (between cell wall and nucleus).

True Statement: The cell membrane encloses the cytoplasm and nucleus, separates one cell from another, and is porous — allowing entry of essential materials and exit of waste.
False 1: The cell wall encloses the cytoplasm and nucleus, and is porous — allowing entry of essential materials and exit of waste.
False 2: The cell membrane is impermeable and does not allow the passage of any materials.

True Statement: Cytoplasm contains carbohydrates, proteins, fats, and mineral salts; most life processes take place within the cytoplasm.
False 1: Cytoplasm contains carbohydrates, proteins, fats, and mineral salts; most life processes take place within the nucleus.
False 2: The nucleus contains carbohydrates, proteins, fats, and mineral salts; most life processes take place within the nucleus.

True Statement: The nucleus regulates all activities within the cell and regulates growth.
False 1: The cytoplasm regulates all activities within the cell and regulates growth.

True Statement: The cell wall (in plant cells) provides rigidity and strength to plants.
False 1: The cell membrane (in plant cells) provides rigidity and strength to plants.

True Statement: Plant cells have tiny rod-shaped structures called plastids; those containing chlorophyll (like chloroplasts) are green and help in photosynthesis.
False 1: Animal cells have tiny rod-shaped structures called plastids containing chlorophyll that help in photosynthesis.
False 2: Plant cells have vacuoles that contain chlorophyll and help in photosynthesis.

True Statement: Plant cells have a large vacuole that helps store important substances, remove waste, and maintain the shape of the cell.
False 1: Animal cells have a large vacuole that helps store important substances, remove waste, and maintain shape.

True Statement: In animal cells, vacuoles are usually absent; if present, they are usually small.
False 1: In plant cells, vacuoles are usually absent; if present, they are usually small.

True Statement: A muscle cell is spindle-shaped, while a nerve cell is very long and has branches.
False 1: A nerve cell is spindle-shaped, while a muscle cell is very long and has branches.

True Statement: Nerve cells (neurons) carry messages in the body; their elongated shape and branched structure help them reach different parts of the body quickly.
False 1: Muscle cells carry messages in the body; their spindle shape helps them reach different parts of the body quickly.

True Statement: The yolk of an ostrich egg is a single cell — the largest known cell — measuring about 130 mm to 170 mm in diameter.
False 1: The yolk of an ostrich egg is the largest known cell, measuring about 1 to 2 mm in diameter.

True Statement: The levels of organisation of life are: Cell → Tissue → Organ → Organ system → Organism.
False 1: The levels of organisation of life are: Cell → Organ → Tissue → Organ system → Organism.

True Statement: A group of similar cells forms a tissue; different tissues form an organ; several organs form an organ system; all organ systems make up an organism.
False 1: A group of similar cells forms an organ; different organs form a tissue; several tissues form an organ system.

True Statement: The life of multicellular organisms begins from a single cell — the egg.
False 1: The life of multicellular organisms begins from a cluster of cells, not a single cell.

True Statement: Microorganisms are too small to be seen with the naked eye and can only be seen under a microscope.
False 1: Microorganisms are small but can be seen with the naked eye without any instrument.

True Statement: Some microorganisms are unicellular (bacteria, Amoeba); others are multicellular (some fungi and algae).
False 1: Bacteria are multicellular; fungi and algae are unicellular.

True Statement: Microorganisms are found in water, soil, air, and even inside our bodies.
False 1: Microorganisms are found only in water and soil, not in air or inside the body.

True Statement: Some microorganisms can survive in extreme conditions such as hot water springs and snow-cold zones.
False 1: No microorganism can survive in extreme conditions such as hot water springs or snow-cold zones.

True Statement: Viruses are microscopic and acellular; they multiply only when they enter a living cell and can infect plants, animals, or bacterial cells.
False 1: Viruses are unicellular microorganisms that can reproduce outside a host cell.
False 2: Viruses can reproduce on their own without entering any host cell.

True Statement: Bacteria do not have a well-defined nucleus; instead they have a nucleoid region.
False 1: Bacteria have a well-defined nucleus just like plant and animal cells.
False 2: Fungi do not have a well-defined nucleus; instead they have a nucleoid region.

True Statement: Fungal cells have a cell wall but no chloroplasts, so they cannot make their own food through photosynthesis.
False 1: Fungal cells have chloroplasts and can make their own food through photosynthesis.
False 2: Bacterial cells have chloroplasts but no cell wall.

True Statement: Yeast is a unicellular fungus while mould is a multicellular fungus.
False 1: Yeast is a multicellular fungus while mould is a unicellular fungus.

True Statement: Bacteria and fungi decompose plant and animal waste into simpler, nutrient-rich substances — a process called decomposition — and recycle nutrients back to the soil.
False 1: Algae decompose plant and animal waste into simpler, nutrient-rich substances through decomposition.
False 2: Bacteria and fungi synthesise complex organic matter from simple nutrients in the soil.

True Statement: Manure formation occurs at optimal temperature and appropriate moisture level.
False 1: Manure formation occurs at any temperature and moisture level without conditions.

True Statement: Some bacteria and fungi live in an oxygen-free environment and decompose plant and animal waste, releasing biogas composed primarily of carbon dioxide and methane.
False 1: Some bacteria and fungi in an oxygen-rich environment release biogas.
False 2: Decomposing bacteria release oxygen and nitrogen as biogas.

True Statement: Biogas is used as a fuel for cooking, heating, generating electricity, and even running vehicles.
False 1: Biogas is used only for cooking and heating, not for generating electricity or running vehicles.

True Statement: Ananda Mohan Chakrabarty developed a special bacterium in 1971 that could break down oil spills; the discovery received a patent in 1980.
False 1: Ananda Mohan Chakrabarty developed a special bacterium in 1980; the discovery received a patent in 1971.
False 2: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek developed a special bacterium that could break down oil spills.

True Statement: Yeast is a type of fungus that grows well in warm conditions; it releases carbon dioxide (making dough soft and fluffy) and a small amount of alcohol during respiration.
False 1: Yeast is a type of bacterium that grows well in warm conditions.
False 2: Yeast releases lactic acid (making dough soft and fluffy) rather than carbon dioxide.

True Statement: Yeast is used in making breads, cakes, and pastries.
False 1: Lactobacillus is used in making breads, cakes, and pastries.

True Statement: Lactobacillus bacteria help in fermentation of batter for idli and dosa, and dough for bhatura.
False 1: Yeast bacteria help in fermentation of batter for idli and dosa, and dough for bhatura.
False 2: Rhizobium bacteria help in fermentation of batter for idli and dosa.

True Statement: Lactobacillus feeds on the sugar (lactose) in milk, produces lactic acid, and makes curd sour; it grows well in warm conditions.
False 1: Lactobacillus feeds on the sugar in milk and produces alcohol, making curd sour.
False 2: Lactobacillus produces lactic acid but grows best in cold conditions, not warm ones.

True Statement: Rhizobium bacteria form nodules in the roots of legumes (beans, peas, lentils) and trap nitrogen from the air, making it useful for plants.
False 1: Lactobacillus bacteria form nodules in the roots of legumes and trap nitrogen from the air.
False 2: Rhizobium bacteria form nodules in the roots of wheat and rice crops and trap nitrogen from the air.

True Statement: Farmers grow legumes in rotation with other crops to naturally increase nitrogen in the soil.
False 1: Farmers grow wheat in rotation with other crops to naturally increase nitrogen in the soil.

True Statement: Microalgae make their own food using sunlight and release oxygen; they produce more than half of Earth's total oxygen supply.
False 1: Microalgae produce less than 10 per cent of Earth's total oxygen supply.
False 2: Bacteria produce more than half of Earth's total oxygen supply.

True Statement: Some microalgae (Spirulina, Chlorella, Diatoms) are used as health supplements and medicines.
False 1: Some microbes (Rhizobium, Lactobacillus) are used as health supplements and medicines.

True Statement: Spirulina is rich in protein — more than 60 per cent of its body weight.
False 1: Spirulina contains less than 20 per cent protein by body weight.
